overview: This two-page file-index document inventories State Department papers on petroleum in the Kwantung Leased Territory, chiefly consular despatches from Dairen to the U.S. Embassy in Tokyo. The entries trace the development of Dairen’s petroleum industry from 1935 through 1938, including the oil monopoly, the refinery at Kanseishi, crude-oil procurement, imports and shipments, foreign suppliers’ responses, and Soviet interest in Dairen’s oil supplies. It also records correspondence concerning an offer by the Export Petroleum Company of California to the Manchuria Oil Company and refers retrospectively to a letter of November 16, 1934.

subfiles.title: List of papers concerning petroleum in the Kwantung Leased Territory

subfiles.about: A two-page index lists correspondence and consular reports concerning the petroleum monopoly, refinery operations, supplies, and trade in Dairen and Manchuria.
subfiles.summary: The first page records correspondence about an offer by the Export Petroleum Company of California to the Manchuria Oil Company and summarizes Dairen reports on the oil monopoly, foreign-company reactions, the local refinery, and new crude-oil shipments during 1935. The continuation lists reports from late 1935 through May 1938 on refinery supplies and output, the Texas Company’s attitude toward the monopoly, petroleum imports, Soviet interest in Dairen’s supplies, and oil production in Manchuria. Many entries note that copies were also indexed under decimal-file subject 893.6363 for Manchuria.

interest: The index offers a compact chronology of the emergence and operation of the Dairen petroleum monopoly and refinery during the consolidation of Japanese-controlled Manchukuo. It is especially useful for locating reports on refinery inputs and outputs, foreign oil-company strategies, and Soviet commercial interest, while its cross-references reveal how the State Department distributed closely related material between its Kwantung Leased Territory and Manchuria files. The Greatwood entry also documents an American oil-company representative’s attempt to investigate the monopoly firsthand.
